news.title: Sandro Mazzola has died at 83: Inter and Italian football remember him
news.lede: The football world mourns Sandro Mazzola, who has died at the age of 83. By a twist of fate, Saturday 19 September marks the 100th anniversary of the inauguration of San Siro, the ground that staged a Milan derby won 6-3 by Inter. San Siro was his lifelong home, where he played for two decades from 1957 to 1977, the first three seasons in the youth team. He scored 158 goals in 565 matches for the first team in the Nerazzurri shirt, the only one he wore in his career.

news.title: Russia handed partial international football return as FIFA includes youth team in Under-15 World Cup draw
news.lede: World football’s governing body has taken a significant step toward reintegrating Russia into the international fold after including their youth side in a new tournament. The move marks the first major softening of the stance against the nation since the widespread sporting ban was implemented four years ago. Russia have officially returned to the international football fold at youth level after being included in the group-stage draw for the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan. Placed in a six-team pool alongside Turkey, Afghanistan, Djibouti, Sierra Leone, and Sudan, the decision marks the first easing of sporting sanctions against the nation since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

news.title: VAR under scrutiny as technology’s role in football expands
news.lede: Another domestic football season is underway, and already, in mid-September, the shortcomings of technology in sport are at the centre of the discourse once again. The video assistant referee (VAR) is perhaps the most discussed technology in modern sport. While video replays have been in use for years in sports like American football, rugby or cricket, it has only been a decade since the International Football Association Board (IFAB), the highest regulatory authority in the sport, approved the use of VAR. With artificial intelligence (AI) reportedly reaching dangerous levels of development and technological optimisation of people's lives at an all-time high, it is perhaps a pertinent time to consider the use of technology in sport.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel admits Kobbie Mainoo's World Cup omission 'hurt' him
news.lede: England manager Thomas Tuchel has admitted it “hurt” him that Kobbie Mainoo did not get a single minute at the FIFA World Cup 2026. The Manchester United midfielder has been recalled for the upcoming Nations League fixtures, with Tuchel saying it is now his responsibility to give the 21-year-old an opportunity.Mainoo was part of England’s World Cup squad but remained an unused substitute throughout the tournament. Speaking after naming his latest squad on Friday, Tuchel explained why he preferred Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson in midfield and why Mainoo would have played in the third-place match against France had he not been injured.“. news.title: Great perplexed by Popovic’s ‘strange’ axing of Socceroos skipper
news.lede: Updated September 18, 2026 - 11.31pm. First published at 1.12am. Mark Bosnich cannot understand the “strange” omission of Mat Ryan for the Socceroos after he failed to make the 26-player squad for the side’s upcoming friendlies against Brazil. Tony Popovic named seven uncapped players in his line-up for the games later this month, while 16 members of his impressive World Cup squad were recalled.

news.title: No. 20 Tigers celebrate Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary
news.lede: Mizzou football (2-0, 0-0 SEC) is back at home this week to host Troy (2-0, 0-0 SBC) for the Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary game at 6 p.m. The 20th-ranked team will celebrate the 100th anniversary of Memorial Stadium by wearing special throwback uniforms on the field, according to Mizzou Athletics. The uniforms will bring back Tiger nostalgia, combining elements from several areas of Mizzou football including the 1920's-style "M' on the jersey, 1970's-inspired sleeve stripes and a narrow Block M with a gray facemask reminiscent of the helmet design introduced in 1971, according to Mizzou Athletics. The helmets front bumper will display the six Columns of Francis Quadrangle, while the pants will represent the historic shade of gold worn by the Tigers through the 20th century, according to Mizzou Athletics.
